specPoints.text: know that: • the universe is a large collection of billions of galaxies • a galaxy is a large collection of billions of stars • our solar system is in the Milky Way galaxy

primer.text: Cosmology has a ladder of scale: billions of galaxies make up the universe, billions of stars make up each galaxy, and one ordinary star — the Sun — anchors our own solar system inside the Milky Way. Keep the three levels straight and every 'place it in the hierarchy' question becomes easy marks.

lessons.title: The universe and galaxies
lessons.opening: The universe is the entirety of space and everything in it — a vast collection of billions of galaxies. Each galaxy, in turn, gathers billions of stars into one vast assembly — enormous glowing objects like the Sun populate it.
keyPoints: Billions of galaxies, gathered together, make up the universe — the largest scale of all.
The universe is also the name for the entirety of space.
Galaxies gather billions of stars into one vast assembly.
Stars are huge glowing spheres of gas, like the Sun.

low.restatement: Universe = billions of galaxies; galaxy = billions of stars.
low.analogy: Cities and countries: stars are houses, galaxies are cities, the universe is the whole planet of cities.
low.examPointer: Definition questions want the 'billions' wording on both levels — quote it.

medium.restatement: Two nested collections define the ladder: stars within galaxies, galaxies within the universe, which also names all of space.
medium.analogy: A Russian doll set: each layer holds many of the layer below, and the outermost doll is the universe.
medium.examPointer: Smallest-to-largest ordering questions are near-guaranteed marks: star, galaxy, universe.

options.text: a large collection of billions of galaxies
options.explanation: Galaxies are the building blocks of the universe.

options.text: a large collection of billions of stars
options.explanation: That defines a galaxy, one level down.
That describes a solar system, two levels down.
A star is far smaller than any galaxy.

options.text: a large collection of billions of stars
options.explanation: Billions of stars bound together form a galaxy.

options.text: a large collection of billions of galaxies
options.explanation: That is the universe.
That is a planetary system.
Galaxies are star collections, not the gaps.

check.stem: Rank star, galaxy and universe — which ordering of scale runs smallest to largest?

options.explanation: Stars collect into galaxies; galaxies collect into the universe.
Stars are smaller than galaxies.
That is largest to smallest.
The universe is the largest level, not the middle.

options.text: huge glowing spheres of gas, like the Sun
options.explanation: The Sun is a typical star.
Moons orbit planets; stars anchor systems.
Stars sit inside galaxies, not the reverse.

options.text: objects made of rock and ice
options.explanation: That describes comets and asteroids.

check.stem: The universe is also the name for…

options.explanation: Beyond the object count, 'universe' names all of space.
Our galaxy is one of billions.
The atmosphere is a thin shell around one planet.
The Solar System is a single system inside one galaxy.

check.modelAnswer: Billions of galaxies, gathered together, make up the universe; the word also names the entirety of space.
A galaxy gathers billions of stars into one vast assembly.

check.stem: Explain why a galaxy is not the same thing as the universe.
check.modelAnswer: A galaxy is one collection of billions of stars, while the universe is the collection of billions of such galaxies — the universe contains many galaxies, so the two sit on different levels of scale.

check.stem: An alien astronomer counts from inside one galaxy. State the two nested collections its home galaxy belongs to.
check.modelAnswer: Its galaxy is one of the billions of galaxies in the collection of galaxies that forms the universe.

lessons.title: Our solar system
lessons.opening: Our solar system sits inside the Milky Way galaxy. The Sun — a star — sits at its centre, and Earth ranks third among the eight planets orbiting it.
keyPoints: Our Solar System is part of the Milky Way galaxy.
The Sun, a star, sits at the centre of our Solar System.
Earth ranks third among the Solar System's eight planets.
In a planetary system, planets and other objects orbit a central star.

low.restatement: Sun at the centre, Earth third of eight planets, all inside the Milky Way.
low.analogy: A house (Earth) on one street (Solar System) in one city (Milky Way) on a whole continent of cities (universe).
low.examPointer: 'Third of eight planets' is the exact phrase examiners look for.

medium.restatement: Containment runs planet → planetary system → galaxy → universe, with the Sun as the system's central star.
medium.analogy: A passenger (Earth) in a car (Solar System) in a car park (galaxy) in a city of car parks (universe).
medium.examPointer: Hierarchy questions fail when students put the galaxy inside the solar system — drill the containment direction.

options.explanation: The galaxy holds billions of stars.

check.stem: State which galaxy contains our Solar System.
check.modelAnswer: The Milky Way galaxy contains our Solar System.

check.stem: State the Earth's position among the Solar System's planets.
check.modelAnswer: It comes third among the eight planets.

check.stem: Explain why the Sun, not the Earth, is the centre of our system.
check.modelAnswer: A planetary system is organised around its central star: the Sun is that star, and the Earth is one of the planets orbiting it, so the Sun sits at the centre.

check.stem: A quiz lists 'Milky Way, Sun, universe, Earth, Solar System'. Order them from smallest to largest.
check.modelAnswer: Earth (a planet) → Solar System (planets orbiting the Sun) → Milky Way (the galaxy holding that system) → universe (the collection of billions of galaxies).

glossary.definition: The entirety of space: billions of galaxies gathered into one whole.
A large collection of billions of stars, such as the Milky Way.
The planets and other objects orbiting our central star, the Sun.
